page: Microsoft Azure E4_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Ev4 server family. It is configured with 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and utilizes an x86_64 architecture. No local storage or GPU resources are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores fall within the average range. However, multi-core CPU benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, are positioned in the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations on large blocks also register in the bottom 25 percent, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is in the bottom 10 percent.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4_v4 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high-throughput processing. The primary tradeoffs include the lack of local storage, which necessitates external network-attached storage, and the lower multi-core efficiency and memory bandwidth.

This instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications that do not require high parallel CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include relational databases relying on external storage, in-memory caching systems with moderate throughput requirements, and enterprise applications that benefit from a larger memory footprint without needing extensive multi-threaded compute power.
